name: Florida
nameStory: Florida is named after Easter. Ponce de Leon made landfall around Easter 1513, which Spaniards call 'Pascua Florida,' the Feast of Flowers, so he called the place La Florida - the flowery land.
capitalStory: Tallahassee is Muskogee for 'old fields,' land the Apalachee had already farmed and left. It became the capital by pure geometry: in 1824 riders set out from St. Augustine and Pensacola, the only two real cities, and the government was planted where they met.

majorFeatures.name: Everglades
majorFeatures.note: A river of grass 60 miles wide and inches deep

majorFeatures.name: Lake Okeechobee
majorFeatures.note: Florida's inland sea, source of the Everglades

majorFeatures.name: St. Johns River
majorFeatures.note: One of the few US rivers that flows north

funFacts: St. Augustine, founded in 1565, is the oldest continuously occupied European settlement in the United States.
No point in Florida is more than about 70 miles from salt water.
The Everglades is the only place on Earth where alligators and crocodiles live side by side.
Its highest point, Britton Hill at 345 feet, is the lowest state high point in the country.
whyItMatters: Florida sits on porous limestone, so rising seawater seeps up through the ground and seawalls cannot stop it. Miami already floods on sunny days at king tide, and salt is pushing into the aquifer the region drinks from.
